newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK SHARES SLIGHTLY HIGHER IN MIXED TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TURK SHARES SLIGHTLY HIGHER IN MIXED TRADE.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended barely higher in mixed trade on Tuesday as the market faced fresh resistance after the recent sharp rallies amid continuing political uncertainty and the prospect of snap elections, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 .XU100 closed four points, or 0.24 percent firmer at 1,659 after falling from an early high of 1,672 on profit-taking. Trade volume dropped to 28.18 trillion lira from Monday's 31.97 trillion.

The index soared 3.76 percent on Monday, disregarding the possibility of snap polls in 1997, after last week's 8.7 percent rally on hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the troubled Islamist-conservative coalition.

"There (is a) need for more liquidity inflow for the index to pierce the 1,650-1,700 band. If there is a positive political development, it may overcome 1,700," said Mehmet Muderrisoglu from Taib investment.
The 1,700 level is also the all-time high close set on January 27.

Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan announced on Sunday he would go to early elections to solve a dispute over religious activism, which has shaken his coalition with pro-Western conservative True Path Party (DYP).
No date has yet been set, although a senior DYP member has said polls would be held by the end of this year. A general election would normally be due by 2000.
Erbakan on Tuesday made clear his conditions for a plan to swap jobs with his coalition partner Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller by the end of June in the run-up to elections.
He said his Islamist Welfare Parth (RP) and Ciller's DYP had to fix the timing of the elections and work together to produce election legislation acceptable to parliament.
Under Turkish law parliament must set the date for elections with a majority vote. The coalition has 274 seats in the 550-member parliament, with two seats vacant.

Analysts say even some government deputies may vote against early polls after only two years in office on fears they may not be reelected. The inability to pass an election law might give the secularist opposition the chance to set up a new coalition.

Of the 244 shares traded, 101 declined, 84 advanced and 59 finished unchanged. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.66 percent to 1,528, the IMKB Services lost 1.35 percent to 1,607 and the IMKB Financial edged 0.16 percent higher to 1,845.
Leading actives were largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, up 7,000 lira at 72,000 and national carrier Turkish Airlines, up 1,500 lira at 39,500. They made up 23.6 percent of the total turnover.
